historical_growth.revenue_note: Continuing (ex-Spain) basis: FY2022 39,127 -> FY2025 40,396 = 1.1% 3yr; FY2020 42,270 (incl. Spain) -> FY2025 40,396 would read -0.9% but is a scope break, so the 5yr figure uses FY2020 ex-Spain estimate ~38.8bn -> 0.8%. The sanity check's 'through-cycle revenue CAGR 0.04%' is the unadjusted reported series across the FY2023 Spain deconsolidation and is not a like-for-like growth rate; the 1.5% selected rate is on the continuing pro-forma perimeter and is retained.
historical_growth.eps_note: Reported EPS is noise (FY2021 impairment, FY2023 Spain deconsolidation, FY2025 GEPP charge): 0.73 -> 0.14 over 3 years. FY2025 normalised: 538m attributable + 1,182m GEPP after tax (1,593 pre-tax x (1-25.8%)) + 332m non-deductible Orange Business impairment = ~2,052m = EUR 0.77/share, vs 0.82 FY2024. H1 2026 adjusted EPS 0.34, +10.9%.
historical_growth.equity_note: Shareholders' equity 34,395 (FY2020) -> 29,739 (FY2025); includes ~4.5-5.0bn of subordinated notes. Payout exceeds attributable earnings in one-off years; book value is not the growth anchor for a telecom - growth is taken from EBITDAaL guidance and segment mix instead.
historical_growth.fcf_note: Company 'free cash flow all-in from telecom activities' (post-SBC, SBC immaterial): 3,058 (FY2022) -> 3,653 (FY2025) = 6.1% 3yr; not available on a consistent ex-Spain basis before FY2022. Organic cash flow guided to ~4.3bn FY2026 and ~5.2bn by 2028.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Blended segment judgment: Africa & Middle East (~18% of pro-forma revenue) growing ~8-10% cb with FX drag, Europe +3-4%, Spain +1-3%, France ~0-1%, Orange Business -3%; FY2025 group +0.5% cb, H1 2026 +2.1% cb (+3.0% underlying).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-2.9%) diverges from revenue (+0.8%) and FCF (+6.1%) by far more than 30% - driven by impairments, the Spain deconsolidation and dividends above reported earnings, not by operating decline. Flagged; not used as the growth anchor.

scenario_narratives.base: Orange delivers the 'Trust the future' plan roughly as guided: pro-forma revenue grows ~1.5-1.8% a year, decelerating to 1% - Africa & Middle East (double-digit cb growth for 11+ quarters, with FX translation drag) and Europe (+3-4%) offset a flat France and an Orange Business segment still shrinking ~3%. EBITDAaL margin expands ~1.9pp over five years as MasOrange's >=500m run-rate synergies land, the French 600m cost programme is sustained and the mix tilts to Africa; this is what >4% EBITDAaL growth on ~2% revenue means. Capex intensity steps down from 16.8% to 16% as the French fibre build completes; spectrum renewals stay in the flows. Cash tax at 23%. Net debt/EBITDAaL drifts from 2.4x back toward 2x by 2028 on ~5bn of organic cash flow, funding the EUR 0.79 -> 0.85 dividend path. SFR is treated as market-structure support, not as an acquisition. Terminal value is bound by an 11.7x unlevered-FCF cap, which is 4.62x EBITDAaL - Orange's own 10-year average EV/EBITDAaL - rather than today's ~5.4x or the 5.9x the model carried before the sanity check.
scenario_narratives.bull: French market structure repairs: the SFR carve-up clears antitrust (three operators from four), Free's price aggression fades, convergent ARPO keeps rising and wholesale fibre co-financing continues; Spain under full ownership extracts the full MasOrange synergy run-rate and low-single-digit growth; Africa & Middle East compounds at high single digits with Orange Money monetisation and no major devaluation; Orange Business stabilises on cyberdefense and portfolio pruning. Revenue grows 2.5-2.8% near term, EBITDAaL margin reaches ~33.65% (pre-lease 38%), capex intensity falls to 15.5% with low-capex SFR customers and completed fibre; cash tax 22%. Terminal cap 13.2x unlevered FCF (= 5.64x EBITDAaL, the 10-year high), growth 1.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The French four-player price war reignites or the SFR deal is blocked and SFR is instead recapitalised as a price-led challenger; Orange Business keeps declining ~3-5% a year with further impairments; a CFA-zone or Egyptian devaluation knocks Africa's euro contribution; copper decommissioning (1.68bn provision, through 2030) and GEPP restructuring cash costs run above plan; MasOrange synergies disappoint and the integration consumes management. Revenue stalls at zero growth from year 5, EBITDAaL margin slips ~0.7pp, capex stays at 17% of revenue to defend fibre and 5G share, cash tax 25%. Leverage stays above 2.4x, the dividend floor becomes a constraint rather than a promise, and the state shareholder's employment priorities limit cost action. Terminal cap 11.5x unlevered FCF (= 3.76x EBITDAaL, the 10-year low), growth 0.5%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Orange as a levered, low-growth cash machine on a pro-forma basis that already includes MasOrange, using unlevered owner FCF after the full lease charge and spectrum, with every prior claim on the equity - net financial debt, hybrid capital and African minorities - taken off in the bridge exactly once. The question is not growth; it is whether a mature European incumbent at ~5.4x EBITDAaL and a 5.6% dividend yield can hold EBITDAaL margins while leverage is worked back to 2x. The terminal multiple is capped at what the market has actually paid for Orange over the last decade - 3.76x / 4.62x / 5.64x EBITDAaL in bear / base / bull - because no buyer pays Gordon-at-7% for a telecom, and the 15x unlevered-FCF cap first used (5.9x EBITDAaL) was above the 10-year high.
valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_response: WHAT TRIPPED (2026-10-26): the multiples sanity check flagged an implied P/E of 106x on the base IV against a 10-year average of 21.7x; P/B (1.86x vs 10-year max 1.40x) and EV/EBITDA (6.78x vs max 5.64x) were above range but did not trip. Roughly three-quarters of the P/E excess is mechanical: the denominator is FY2025 statutory net income of EUR 538m, which carries the one-off EUR 1,593m GEPP early-retirement charge and a 332m Orange Business impairment that the model already strips from its base. Normalised (538 + 1,182 after-tax GEPP + 332) FY2025 EPS is ~0.77 and the base IV sat at ~27x that - inside the 2x-of-average rule. The residual - P/B and EV/EBITDA above their 10-year maxima - traced to the terminal: the 15x unlevered-FCF cap equalled 5.9x EBITDAaL, higher than any year-end multiple Orange has traded at since 2016. WHAT CHANGED: terminal caps re-anchored to the 10-year EV/EBITDAaL range per the research-stock fix option 4 - bear 3.76x (10-year low), base 4.62x (average), bull 5.64x (high) - expressed in the engine as 11.5x / 11.7x / 13.2x unlevered FCF. No driver path, the WACC, the weights, the SBC treatment or the equity bridge was touched; the 'wacc_too_low' diagnosis was rejected (see wacc_rationale). The mechanical P/E will keep tripping on the statutory FY2025 denominator until the FY2026 actuals roll in; read the normalised figure in sanity_check.implied_multiples_after_fix instead. The cost of the fix is that the base terminal now sits below today's market multiple (~5.4x): if the 2025-26 European telecom re-rating proves durable, this valuation understates Orange by roughly EUR 4 per share.
key_risks_to_valuation: NCI fair value is an estimate (6,000m vs 3,321m book): each 1bn moves value ~EUR 0.38/share
Pro-forma FY0 assumes immaterial Orange/MasOrange intra-group eliminations and MasOrange lease intensity similar to Orange's

Terminal value is cap-bound in every scenario and the caps are anchored to a decade (2016-2025) in which European telecoms de-rated; each 1x of unlevered-FCF cap moves base value by ~EUR 1.35/share, each 0.5x of EBITDAaL by ~EUR 1.7/share
SFR consortium deal: debt-funded, closes H2 2027 at the earliest, subject to French antitrust; modelled only through market-structure margins, not as an acquisition
D&A (16.3% terminal) stays above capex (16.0%) because of acquired-intangible amortisation; the tax shield this implies is partly real and partly PPA - a 0.3pp gap is worth ~EUR 0.1/share
African FX translation: comparable-basis growth exceeded historical-basis growth by ~2.5pp in FY2025
Hybrid notes deducted at carrying value; Orange has been a net issuer (+482m in H1 2026), which substitutes for senior debt rather than adding to the claim stack
FY2025 statutory earnings (EUR 0.14/share) understate run-rate earning power (~0.77 normalised) by the GEPP charge; screens keyed on trailing P/E will misread Orange until FY2026 actuals

sanity_check.fix_applied: 2026-10-26, one pass. P/E trip diagnosed as ~75% denominator artifact (FY2025 statutory NI 538m carries the 1,593m pre-tax GEPP early-retirement charge and 332m OB impairment; normalised NI ~2,052m, EPS ~0.77). Residual (P/B and EV/EBITDA above 10-year maxima) traced to the 15x unlevered-FCF terminal cap = 5.9x EBITDAaL, above the 10-year high. Fix: terminal caps re-anchored to the 10-year EV/EBITDAaL range (research-stock fix option 4): bear 3.76x / base 4.62x / bull 5.64x = 11.5x / 11.7x / 13.2x unlevered FCF. WACC, growth, margins, SBC, bridge and weights unchanged; 'wacc_too_low' and 'growth_too_high' diagnoses rejected (26 regulators, not one; through-cycle CAGR straddles the Spain deconsolidation).

implied_multiples_after_fix.pe_normalised_note: 16.28 / (FY2025 normalised EPS 0.772 - SBC 0.007 = 0.765); vs 10yr average 21.7x and 2x rule 43.4x. Before the fix: 27.2x. The script's mechanical P/E (83.2x after, 106.3x before) divides by statutory FY2025 EPS 0.14, which carries the 1,593m GEPP charge; it will keep tripping until FY2026 actuals replace FY2025 in the denominator.
implied_multiples_after_fix.ev_ebitdaal_note: (16.28 x 2,660.3 + NFD 35,683) / (pro-forma FY2025 EBITDAaL 14,754 - SBC 18); before the fix 5.97x. Inside the 10yr range 3.76x-5.64x. The script's 5.78x (6.78x before) sets June-2026 debt that includes MasOrange against FY2025 EBITDA that excludes it.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 PRO FORMA: Orange telecom activities ex-Spain 40,396 (FY2025 AR) + MasOrange FY2025 revenue 7,601 (FY2025 results presentation p.20, management accounts). MasOrange was equity-accounted until 8 June 2026 and is fully consolidated from then; the June 2026 balance sheet already carries its debt and the EUR 4.25bn purchase price, so the flows must be pro forma too. Intra-group wholesale eliminations between Orange and MasOrange are not disclosed and assumed immaterial. Cross-check: company-disclosed H1 2026 revenue as if consolidated from 1 Jan 2026 = 24.7bn (H1 2026 report Note 3), i.e. ~49bn annualised.
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average diluted shares FY2025: 2,660,272,101 (FY2025 AR line 7077). Held flat: SBC is expensed in the flows (and is immaterial, ~EUR 18m/yr); no non-SBC issuance planned - the SFR consortium deal is guided as debt-financed.
inputs.net_debt_note: Orange's own Net Financial Debt at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 report s.1.5.8 / Note 10.3). Excludes IFRS 16 lease liabilities (consistent with lease treatment B), excludes Mobile Financial Services, includes debt related to financed assets, nets derivatives and other financial assets - which is why it is 2.6bn below gross financial liabilities 47,625 less cash 9,305. Up 13,157 in six months, of which 13,895 is the scope effect of consolidating MasOrange (its ~9.4bn debt plus the 4.25bn paid to Lorca).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 'Free cash flow all-in from telecom activities' (company definition, ex-Spain): after interest, cash tax, lease repayments, licences and hybrid coupons. Informational anchor only - the engine projects UNLEVERED owner FCF from the pro-forma component paths; interest, hybrid coupons, leases and NCI are handled in the bridge / lease line.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income (271m FY2025) is NOT stripped: Orange is a net borrower, the engine's flows are unlevered, and the gross cash pile is already netted inside net financial debt.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR cash-flow statement share-based compensation add-back (18m), kpis StockBasedComp; EquityAwardTaxes nil. Orange is effectively an SBC-zero filer (0.05% of revenue): house and street bases coincide to within cents.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 purchase of treasury shares 11m (FY2025 AR line 358) - employee-plan hedging only, no capital-return programme. Capital return is the dividend: EUR 0.75 for FY2025, EUR 0.79 set for FY2026 (interim 0.30 paid 3 Dec 2026), floor EUR 0.85 by 2028.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:36:10Z regular close (Euronext Paris; Yahoo chart API; 52-week range 13.49-18.805)
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-denominated build. CAPM at market weights gives ~5%: 10y OAT ~3.4%, ERP 5.5%, beta ~0.7 -> cost of equity ~7.3%; after-tax cost of debt ~2.9% (avg coupon ~3.3-3.8%); claims (NFD 35.7bn + hybrids 5.0bn + NCI ~6bn) are ~55% of EV at the current price. House uses 7.0%: Orange's own FY2025 goodwill impairment-test post-tax rates are France 5.9%, Belgium 6.1%, Poland 7.2%, Enterprise 7.3%, Romania 8.5% (FY2025 AR Note 7.3), with Africa & Middle East (~25% of EBITDAaL) undisclosed but necessarily higher on country risk; an EBITDAaL-weighted blend is ~7%, which also sits inside the 6-7.5% range sell-side applies to European incumbents. The Africa country-risk component belongs in the discount rate for those flows and is not a scenario-risk premium. Same WACC across all three scenarios: cyclicality, French price-war and SFR execution risk are charged in the flows and the weights, not stacked on the discount rate. Sanity-check 2026-10-26 offered 'wacc_too_low (regulatory single point of failure)' as a diagnosis; rejected - Orange answers to 26 national regulators, not one, and the loose assumption was the terminal multiple, which was fixed instead (see terminal notes).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B - leases as operating cost. Full lease cash charge (FY2025: repayments of lease liabilities 1,496 + interest paid on lease liabilities 244 = 1,740 = 4.3% of ex-Spain revenue; MasOrange assumed similar intensity) is deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path. D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use (FY2025: fixed assets 7,005 + financed assets 116 = 7,121 = 17.6% of revenue; ROU depreciation 1,428 excluded). Lease liabilities (7,206 non-current + 1,653 current at June 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt, exactly as Orange's NFD definition excludes them. Owner EBITDA in this model therefore equals Orange's EBITDAaL less SBC.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI deducted once, in the equity bridge, at an estimated fair value of 6,000m (~10x the 601m NCI share of FY2025 net income; ~1.8x the 3,321m book value at June 2026; NCI dividends 433m FY2025). Flows are 100% consolidated. The minorities sit mainly in Africa & Middle East (Sonatel ~58% minority, Orange Maroc, Orange Jordan, Orange Egypt partners) where listed multiples and growth justify a premium to book.
inputs.hybrid_treatment: Perpetual subordinated notes 4,993m at June 2026 (balance sheet, Note 12.4) are equity under IFRS and excluded from Orange's NFD; coupons (169m FY2025) are below EBITDAaL and below the engine's flows. They are a prior claim on equity holders and are deducted in the equity bridge at carrying value.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company route, non-US adaptations: EUR WACC, lease treatment B, NCI and hybrid claims in the bridge, matching-asset rule for associates). Orange is a telecom operator, not a utility-like regulated asset or a holdco, so the owner-FCF route is correct; the AFFO/NAV/residual-income routes do not apply. Fresh build - no prior DCF or memory entry. PRO-FORMA BASE: FY0 is FY2025 with MasOrange consolidated for 12 months (see base_revenue_note); the company's own NFD/EBITDAaL ratio uses the same convention (EBITDAaL incl. MasOrange 12 months = 14,846 at June 2026 vs 14,754 in this model's FY0). SFR: the June 2026 MoU (Orange ~27% share, ~5.6bn EV, +1.7bn revenue, +0.6bn EBITDAaL rising to ~0.9bn post-synergies, debt-financed, closing not before H2 2027, antitrust review) is NOT modelled as an acquisition - it is value-neutral-to-mildly-accretive at ~9x EBITDAaL, and its main effect is on French market structure, which is captured in the bull/base margin paths. ONE-OFFS stripped from the base: FY2021 3.7bn impairment; FY2025 1,593m GEPP/TPS early-retirement charge (1,549 in operating income + 44 in finance cost, FY2025 AR employee-benefits note) and 332m Orange Business impairment; H1 2026 2.4bn MasOrange revaluation gain. CAPEX: accounting capex incl. spectrum licences (FY2025 7,322 = 18.1% incl. 640 licences) is modelled, not eCAPEX (15%); the path steps down as French FTTH build completes and MasOrange synergies land. BAND: SBC is ~0.05% of revenue, so house and street values coincide and band_position is degenerate - read it as not applicable. ANALYSIS JSON: read after it landed mid-build (analysis_date 2026-10-26); narratives draw on its bull/bear points. SANITY-CHECK FIX (2026-10-26, one pass): terminal caps re-anchored from 13/15/16x unlevered FCF to the 10-year EV/EBITDAaL range (3.76x / 4.62x / 5.64x = 11.5 / 11.7 / 13.2x unlevered FCF); all driver paths, WACC and weights unchanged.
inputs.guidance_fy2026: Raised at H1 2026 (incl. 7 months of MasOrange): EBITDAaL growth >4% (was >3%); eCAPEX/revenue ~15%; Organic Cash Flow ~EUR 4.3bn (was ~4.0bn); medium-term net debt/EBITDAaL ~2x (2.4x at June 2026). 'Trust the future' 2026-2028 plan (Feb 2026 CMD): Organic Cash Flow toward ~5.2bn by 2028, dividend floor 0.85 by 2028.

bear.terminal_note: Cap 11.5x unlevered FCF = 3.76x year-10 EBITDAaL (14,733 on 4,819 FCF), the 10-year LOW EV/EBITDAaL (FY2020, Covid trough). Was 13x (= 4.25x EBITDAaL). The FCF cap is close to the base case's 11.7x only because bear FCF conversion is worse (17% capex intensity, 25% tax); on EBITDAaL the gap is 3.76x vs 4.62x. Cap binds: Gordon at 7.0%/0.5% would be 15.5x.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-lease EBITDA margin. FY0 pro forma: EBITDAaL 14,754 + lease cash 2,064 = 16,818 = 35.0%. Year-1 35.8% less 4.3% lease less 0.05% SBC = 31.45% EBITDAaL margin -> 15,370, +4.2% on pro-forma FY0, matching the >4% guidance. Matures at 32.65% EBITDAaL (~+1.9pp over 5 years) on MasOrange run-rate synergies (>=500m), the French cost programme and Africa mix.
base.capex_note: Accounting capex incl. spectrum: eCAPEX ~15% guided + ~0.8-1.2% licences + ~0.5% disposal proceeds grossed back. FY2025 was 18.1% incl. a 640m licence year; steps to 16% as French FTTH build ends and MasOrange network synergies land.
base.cash_tax_note: FY2025 cash tax 1,138 on ~5,350 adjusted EBIT = 21%; FY2024 988 on ~5,600 = 18%; statutory France 25.8%, higher in Africa. 23% flat - no carryforward shelter is perpetuated.
base.terminal_note: Cap 11.7x unlevered FCF = 4.62x year-10 EBITDAaL (18,079 ex-lease ex-SBC on 7,137 FCF), Orange's 10-year AVERAGE EV/EBITDAaL ex outliers (sanity_check historical table, FY2018-FY2025: min 3.76x, avg 4.62x, max 5.64x). Re-anchored 2026-10-26 from 15x (= 5.9x EBITDAaL, above anything the market paid for Orange in a decade). Cap binds: Gordon at 7.0%/1.0% would be 16.8x.

bull.terminal_note: Cap 13.2x unlevered FCF = 5.64x year-10 EBITDAaL (20,115 on 8,568 FCF), the 10-year HIGH EV/EBITDAaL (FY2025 year-end, after the 2025 European telecom re-rating). Was 16x (= 6.2x EBITDAaL). Cap binds: Gordon at 7.0%/1.5% would be 18.5x.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 11.7x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: leverage jumped to 2.4x EBITDAaL with a further debt-funded ~5.6bn SFR share pending, French pricing has broken down twice in fifteen years, Orange Business is in structural decline, and the state is the largest shareholder with employment priorities that constrain cost action. Bull cut to 25%: it needs several independent things to go right at once - SFR antitrust clearance, Spanish synergies, no African devaluation and a French price repair - and the French antitrust outcome is binary and outside management's control.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.
